headline: #001 refresh: 4 institutions run from here (2025); 59% of deposits run from elsewhere
question: How has ownership of our banks changed?
measure: At its peak in 1974, 47 banks and thrifts were headquartered in the five counties. In June 2025, 4 remain, and 59¢ of every dollar on deposit sits with an institution run from somewhere else.
method: FDIC institution records and Summary of Deposits, June each year, five counties. 'Run from here' = institution headquartered in the five counties. Caveat: HQ county reflects an institution's final headquarters across its whole history; pre-1989 thrift coverage may be incomplete.
why_it_might_matter: Published figure holds on refresh; no material change since publication.
why_hold: Refresh of a published measure — surface only if the number moved.

headline: #002 refresh: region is 1 in 1,282 of US deposits (2025); was 1 in 494 in 1994
question: Do our deposits matter to the big banks?
measure: In 1994 about 1 in 494 dollars on deposit in US banks was in the five counties; in 2025, about 1 in 1,282. To the holding companies with more than $100 billion in US deposits, the region is about 15¢ of every $100 they hold.
method: FDIC Summary of Deposits, June each year. National banks defined as holding companies with > $100B US deposits in the same year, deposit-weighted (five in 2025: JPMorgan, PNC, Fifth Third, KeyCorp, Huntington). Caveat: this definition gives 15–17¢ depending on year; the published 18¢ likely used a slightly broader set or the 2024 vintage. Fixing the definition makes the figure reproducible.
why_it_might_matter: Published 18¢ reproduces as 15–17¢ under an explicit definition; method note should carry the definition on next refresh.
why_hold: Refresh with a definitional note for the editor, not a new finding.

headline: Share of deposits run from elsewhere peaked at 70% in 2013; now 59%
question: Is control of our deposits still leaving?
measure: In 1994, 23¢ of every dollar on deposit here sat with an institution run from elsewhere. That climbed to 70¢ by 2013. Since then it has come back to 59¢ — the first sustained move toward local control in the record.
method: FDIC Summary of Deposits, June each year 1994–2025, five counties, by institution HQ county. Caveat: the reversal is driven mostly by one institution's growth (1st Source); it is a fact about concentration as much as about localness.
why_it_might_matter: Contradicts the one-directional story #001 implies. The trend since 2010 runs the other way, though it rests on one bank.

headline: Bank branches 219 → 166 since 1994 while deposits grew $6.4B → $14.1B
question: Where did the bank branches go?
measure: Of every 4 bank branches in the five counties in 1994, about 3 remain today (219 → 166). Over the same years, deposits here more than doubled, from $6.4 billion to $14.1 billion.
method: FDIC Summary of Deposits, June 1994 and June 2025, branch counts and deposits for the five counties. Nominal dollars. Caveat: SOD counts reporting offices, which includes some non-retail locations; the branch trend is not adjusted for population.
why_it_might_matter: Physical banking presence is shrinking as money grows — a Destination and Spatial Productivity question nobody has put a number on for the region.

headline: 67¢ of every $1 1st Source holds anywhere is from the five counties
question: How much do our banks depend on us?
measure: Of every dollar 1st Source holds on deposit anywhere, about 67¢ is from the five counties. For the five holding companies over $100 billion, it is about 15¢ of every $100.
method: FDIC Summary of Deposits, June 2025: each holding company's five-county deposits divided by its total US deposits. Caveat: 1st Source's out-of-region branches are recent; this share will fall as they grow, which is itself the thing to watch.
why_it_might_matter: The mirror image of #002. Local banks are exposed to the region in a way national banks structurally cannot be — alignment, and concentration risk, in one number.

headline: Edgewater  Bank (Saint Joseph, MI) ceased as an independent institution on 2021-05-01
why_it_might_matter: A locally headquartered institution left the record; its deposits now sit with an acquirer. One fewer of the '4 that remain' in #001. Holding company at end: EDGEWATER BCORP INC.
why_hold: Historical on first run; future runs surface only new changes.
